content.intro: {state} charges {stateRate} sales tax on a vehicle, with no local sales tax. Registration is paid every year and falls as the vehicle ages, and each county adds its own small administration fees.

howItWorks.text: The state rate is {stateRate}. A trade-in lowers the price the tax is figured on.
If you correctly paid sales tax to a dealer in another state, you get a credit against the Idaho tax.
The yearly registration fee drops as the vehicle gets older, and electric vehicles pay an added yearly fee.
Each county sets its own administration fee for registration and for titles on top of the state fees.

faq.q: Does a trade-in lower the sales tax in Idaho?
faq.text: Yes, a trade-in allowance reduces the taxable price when it is part of the same transaction.

faq.q: Does Idaho give credit for tax paid in another state?
faq.text: Yes, a credit is allowed when sales tax was correctly paid to a dealer in another state.
